transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-03-04 16:00 UTC | Duration: ~52 mins | Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Daniel (Medexa Head of Platform), Lena (Medexa Security), Raj (Medexa IT)

00:00 Speaker 1 (Jordan): hey everyone, thanks for joining, um we'll do a quick intro then dive into the SSO SCIM and RBAC stuff, is that still the right agenda?
00:18 Speaker 2 (Daniel): yep that's right, Daniel here. We're specifically concerned about how Redwood will fit in with our Okta setup, uh and least-privilege for service teams, and also auditability for compliance.
00:35 Speaker 3 (Priya): great, thanks Daniel. quick intros from our side: i'm priya, i'm the se working on integrations, and i'll run through the SAML and SCIM flows and show how roles map. Jordan is your AE and will own proc and next steps.
00:50 Speaker 1 (Jordan): yeah hi all, thanks. quick note: we have SOC 2 and ISO docs available, we'll share a summary. the focus here is mapping your requirements to Redwood's features: SSO via SAML, SCIM for group sync and provisioning, RBAC with least privilege profiles, audit logs, and optional KMS for encryption.
01:10 Speaker 4 (Lena): perfect. first question — does Redwood support IdP-initiated and SP-initiated SAML flows? and how are attributes consumed for RBAC?
01:28 Speaker 2 (Priya): yes we support both, though most customers do SP-initiated for onboarding. attribute-wise we accept typical SAML claims: email, uid, groups, and we can map group names to Redwood roles. small caveat— sometimes the idp sends group IDs instead of names, so we do a mapping layer.
01:48 Speaker 3 (Raj): uh, in our org groups are namespaced like dev-team-a, dev-team-b, and we use Okta SCIM to provision. we want to make sure we can do least-privilege: e.g., only "platform-ops" can deploy or change model routes, devs only have invoke/token scope. can that be modelled?
02:08 Speaker 2 (Priya): absolutely. Redwood's RBAC lets you create granular roles—there's admin, deployer, billing, observer, developer-invoke, and you can create custom roles. you map those to SCIM groups or SAML attributes. for example, map dev-team-a to developer-invoke and map platform-ops to deployer+admin.
02:29 Speaker 1 (Jordan): and to add, we recommend least-privilege by default: start with observer role for new groups, then escalate only for specific users. we'll include a recommended role matrix based on your org's structure.
02:45 Speaker 2 (Lena): ok good. next — SCIM provisioning. does Redwood support group delta syncs and bulk syncs? and what's the cadence? our SCIM uses incremental updates from Okta.
03:05 Speaker 3 (Priya): yes we support SCIM v2, including delta (change) syncs and full syncs, webhooks for provisioning events. typical cadence is near real-time for deltas; polling intervals configurable. one note: SCIM group membership limits — very large groups may require pagination and a slightly different approach.
03:28 Speaker 1 (Daniel): what about deprovisioning? if someone leaves, is access revoked immediately?
03:36 Speaker 3 (Priya): yes, via SCIM removal or SAML assertion change, access can be revoked. we also support a short session timeout option and token revocation for immediate effect, plus audit events for deprovisioning.
03:52 Speaker 2 (Jordan): moving into audit logs — Lena, you said auditability is a primary concern. we capture admin actions, token issuance, model route changes, and user logins. logs are available in console and via our audit log API/stream for SIEM integration.
04:12 Speaker 4 (Lena): retention—how long are logs retained and can we export them? we have policy to keep audit trails for two years for certain data classes.
04:22 Speaker 3 (Priya): default retention is 90 days in the console, but enterprise plan can push to your S3 or syslog for long-term retention and archiving. we can stream to your SIEM (Splunk, Sumo, etc.) or push encrypted archives to an S3 bucket in your account.
04:40 Speaker 4 (Lena): okay we'll want to use our S3 with KMS keys if possible. what's the KMS story?
04:48 Speaker 3 (Priya): Redwood supports customer-managed keys (CMK) in major clouds and HSM-backed keys via partnerships. we can integrate with your KMS so that at-rest encryption keys are under your control for the private deployment or dedicated setups. hosted/shared deployments have provider-managed keys by default but enterprise customers can opt into CMK.
05:08 Speaker 1 (Daniel): data residency — our prod data must remain in us-east-1. can we guarantee that?
05:16 Speaker 3 (Priya): yes, region pinning is available for Dedicated and Private — you can pin data and inference to a region. hosted API customers on standard plan might see multi-region routing for resilience; for Medexa's requirements we recommend Dedicated or Private.
05:32 Speaker 4 (Raj): one of our engineers asked about service accounts — we want machine-to-machine auth for model calls without a human user. how do you handle that with RBAC?
05:42 Speaker 3 (Priya): we support service accounts with scoped tokens. you can attach policies to service accounts that grant only the invoke/model access and not admin or billing. tokens can be short-lived with refresh and audited separately.
06:00 Speaker 2 (Jordan): Priya can you walk through an example SAML assertion and how group claims get mapped?
06:06 Speaker 3 (Priya): sure — rough example: assertion contains: subject->email, attr: groups:["dev-team-a","platform-ops"], role: maybe "engineer". Redwood imports groups and then applies mapping rules — e.g., if groups contains "platform-ops" then grant role deployer; else if groups contains dev-team-a grant developer-invoke. we also support attribute-based rules and regex matching for groups.
06:36 Speaker 4 (Lena): there's sometimes noise in attributes — our idp sends group IDs as guids. can you support mapping via an external lookup?
06:45 Speaker 3 (Priya): yes, we support a mapping table and you can provide a transform script or we'll do the mapping on onboarding. we can also rely on SCIM to sync human-readable names if your Okta is authoritative.
06:58 Speaker 1 (Daniel): what about provisioning groups into Redwood — do we create roles in Redwood automatically when SCIM sync creates a group?
07:06 Speaker 3 (Priya): by default SCIM creates users and groups as placeholders; we recommend a staged approach where groups are provisioned but privileges are mapped after review. auto-role assignment is configurable — you can choose to auto-map or require admin approval.
07:22 Speaker 4 (Raj): fine. security question — do you support SAML signing cert rotation and how do we rotate keys without downtime?
07:31 Speaker 3 (Priya): yes we support multiple certificates and a rollover process: upload new cert, test in parallel, then flip. we also support metadata URL consumption for automated refresh from some IdPs.
07:44 Speaker 2 (Jordan): another point — for least-privilege we suggest starting with a conservative mapping doc. I'll send a matrix with role definitions and suggested mappings for Medexa by the end of the week.
07:58 Speaker 4 (Lena): good. compliance — can you share SOC 2 and ISO attestation? also pen test reports?
08:06 Speaker 3 (Priya): we can share our SOC 2 Type II and ISO summary under an NDA. pen test summaries are available; full reports usually under stricter controls. we'll attach those to the email.
08:20 Speaker 2 (Daniel): regarding logs — are admin actions write-once? tamper-evident? we need chain-of-custody for forensics.
08:30 Speaker 3 (Priya): logs are append-only in our internal system and we support pushing to your S3 with immutable object lock if you want tamper-evidence. for the highest assurance we recommend pushing logs into your retention system under your KMS.
08:48 Speaker 4 (Lena): nice. a bit on onboarding — what's the fastest path to test SAML+SCIM with a small pilot?
08:57 Speaker 3 (Priya): typical pilot: 1) send SAML metadata and SCIM endpoint + token to your IdP admin, 2) test SP-initiated login with a handful of users, 3) provision a couple of groups via SCIM, 4) run role mapping and smoke tests. that usually takes a few hours to a couple days depending on IdP availability.
09:18 Speaker 1 (Jordan): we'll do that. we'll also need someone from your IdP side for the workshop — can you confirm who will join?
09:26 Speaker 4 (Daniel): lena and raj will join and our Okta admin samir will try to make the workshop.
09:33 Speaker 2 (Priya): perfect. any questions about private deployment versus dedicated for these requirements?
09:40 Speaker 4 (Daniel): cost tradeoffs — we heard dedicated gives region pinning and CMK but it's more expensive; private is heavier lift but we get full VPC control. from security side, dedicated could be enough if we can control KMS and log egress.
09:58 Speaker 3 (Priya): yep that's accurate. we usually recommend Dedicated for teams wanting managed infra but strict controls (KMS, S3-to-your-account archives). Private is for air-gapped or very strict network restrictions. we'll provide a comparison doc.
10:15 Speaker 1 (Jordan): quick callouts — SCIM rate limits, group size caveats, and token rotation policies. we'll document these in the guide.
10:26 Speaker 4 (Lena): one last technical — do you support just-in-time provisioning for external contractors? they want ephemeral access for 30 days.
10:35 Speaker 3 (Priya): yes we support JIT and expiry policies for auto-provisioned users; you can set max lifetime and require re-auth or re-approval after expiry.
10:46 Speaker 2 (Jordan): great, let's summarize next steps — i'll send the initial email with the SAML metadata template, priya will attach SOC2 and logs doc, and we'll schedule the SCIM/RBAC workshop around 2026-03-15. any other asks?
11:07 Speaker 4 (Daniel): pls also include recommended role matrix and example regex mappings for our group names.
11:15 Speaker 3 (Priya): noted, we'll include examples.
11:22 Speaker 1 (Jordan): awesome, thanks everyone. we'll follow up by Friday.
11:27 Speaker 4 (Lena): thanks, bye.

Notes: transcript has minor recognition errors in names and acronyms; intermittent filler words preserved. Links shared during call: "Redwood SSO Guide (link)" , "SOC2 summary (secure link)", "SCIM mapping template (sheet)".

End of transcript.
